1.translation: Examples use bundled tables or small installed files. Each block identifies the packages it uses.

4.translation: Bundled ⟦shared:0⟧ already retains real characters, physical header line numbers and source-file provenance; use ⟦shared:1⟧ when importing your own FASTA. Import removes whitespace while retaining case; declare bp or aa explicitly rather than guessing the alphabet. Focusing clips both strings and intervals: local position 1 below corresponds to source position 1001. Descending regions select the same interval without reverse-complementing it. Lengths alone cannot recover characters, and HSP endpoints cannot recover mismatch or gap columns. Gapped FASTA lengths include gaps; genomic use needs a separate alignment-column-to-source-position mapping.

7.translation: The bundled cactus FASTA contains equal-length aligned records. Replace the file path to read your own alignment.

10.translation: ## Existing alignments: keep columns and source positions separate ⟦shared:0⟧

11.translation: The examples directly use prepared DNA/protein alignment tables in ⟦shared:0⟧. Original Biopython records, upstream licenses, hashes and reproducible FASTA conversion rules remain in the source directory ⟦shared:1⟧. No alignment tools are run and complete record IDs and original characters are unchanged; rows and columns are selected explicitly.

12.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reads one existing alignment. Declare DNA, RNA or AA; equal lengths alone do not establish homology. ⟦shared:1⟧ includes ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧ gaps, whose ⟦shared:4⟧ is NA. Default positions count the ungapped input fragment from one; they are not complete-genome coordinates. Lowercase letters consume positions, so this reader must not be used as an A3M insertion parser.

14.translation: The first selected row has a gap at alignment column 343. Column lookup therefore returns ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and a missing source position. Inverse lookup of source position 343 finds its actual alignment column, without interpolation. Positions removed by filtering return ⟦shared:2⟧; filtering never renumbers retained columns. ⟦shared:3⟧ selects an alignment-row ID even when a separately declared source ID differs.

15.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ is a standard Cartesian ggplot layer. Styles and user scales follow ggplot2. It measures glyphs against actual cell width and height at draw time: ⟦shared:1⟧ requires readable letters; ⟦shared:2⟧ retains colour cells where text cannot fit, without shrinking fonts. Focus fewer columns or increase physical width to show letters. For example, save ⟦shared:4⟧ with ordinary ⟦shared:3⟧; simply raising DPI adds no physical room. Discrete rows, identity/reverse position scales and Cartesian coordinates are supported; this layer does not directly project characters onto backbone Coords. A Cartesian character plot with explicit source mapping can be registered using ⟦shared:5⟧ for [Fusion character details](⟦shared:6⟧).

16.translation: Default residue plots join neighbouring cells continuously and use a 1:1 cell ratio unless coordinates were explicitly supplied. Dark bold sans-serif glyphs fit the cells at a uniform size, with a default readability floor of 3 mm. Without an explicit fill, label is mapped automatically and the data alphabet selects DNA/RNA/AA chemistry colours. Use ⟦shared:0⟧ to select an alphabet or ⟦shared:1⟧ to replace the colours. Explicit sizes, mappings, fixed colours and user coordinates take priority. Character legends are hidden by default; enable them with ⟦shared:2⟧.

18.translation: Pass ⟦shared:0⟧ to ⟦shared:1⟧ to display 100 bases as lines 1–50 and 51–100. This example reads the first 100 observed bases of MT108731.1. Row labels retain the original column ranges and the x axis shows the column within a line. Multiple sequences share the same breaks, and gaps still occupy columns. Original data, alignment columns and source positions are not renumbered.

20.translation: ![100 observed bases displayed as two lines of 50 columns](⟦shared:0⟧)

21.translation: Wrapped character plots can also be registered for Fusion. Each focus interval must fit within one displayed line; split cross-line selections into explicit source intervals. The default ⟦shared:0⟧ is NULL, which keeps a single line.

24.translation: The same data contract accepts observed protein characters. The excerpt retains upstream gaps and residue differences; default fill groups amino acids by side-chain chemistry, rather than inferred functional domains.

28.translation: Provide one ⟦shared:0⟧ row per aligned record with ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧. ⟦shared:2⟧ is the first nongap source coordinate. Negative-strand positions decrease; strings must already be in alignment orientation. An optional ⟦shared:4⟧ identifies the original molecule. If you provide a full forward ⟦shared:5⟧, every nongap character is checked, using nucleotide complementation on the negative strand and order reversal only for AA. Missing source strings remain unverified; no origins or strands are guessed.

29.translation: The following example checks consistency against ungapped fragments derived from the same alignment. It is deliberately **not independent genomic validation**. For a real genomic projection, supply independently known source sequences and interval metadata instead.

31.translation: No mismatch/gap detail can be recovered from six HSP endpoints alone. This workflow accepts existing columns, not CIGAR/A3M/Clustal/Stockholm parsing, phase inference, consensus/Logo analysis or alignment computation. Explicit CDS translation is described below; exact macro/detail registration is available in the Fusion section.

34.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ defines observed coding coordinates; ⟦shared:1⟧ additionally needs actual complete forward DNA/RNA strings and optional **Biostrings**. This real EMALE negative-strand CDS has source phase 0 and an ATG start. Table 11 is an explicit choice checked against the unchanged upstream protein FASTA. Input provenance is in ⟦shared:2⟧.

36.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reports coding/protein strings, genetic code, initiation/ambiguity policies, partial ends and terminal remainder. ⟦shared:1⟧ retains each genomic base; ⟦shared:2⟧ contains the three genomic positions of each codon in biological order, even across exon boundaries. Residue positions use the CDS feature ID's observed-protein namespace; they are not an inferred external protein accession. Terminal and internal stops remain ⟦shared:3⟧. The example removes only the final stop for comparison with the upstream FASTA convention.

37.translation: The default ⟦shared:0⟧ does not recode alternative starts; ⟦shared:1⟧ requires a complete 5-prime end. ⟦shared:2⟧ rejects fuzzy codons; explicit ⟦shared:3⟧ delegates to Biostrings, using X if unresolved. Unknown codes, missing/short sources and declared translation exceptions fail. ⟦shared:4⟧ belongs to the CDS map: only the initial phase and incomplete terminal codon are excluded; later segment phases validate continuity without deleting junction bases. No missing sequence is reconstructed. RNA must be declared explicitly. Ordered ⟦shared:5⟧ support the existing spliced/origin-join contract.

38.translation: A complete runnable nucleotide/codon/macro example is ⟦shared:0⟧; its negative-strand labels are centred on their three coding bases. Real spliced plus/minus controls, source hashes and original expected translations are retained in ⟦shared:1⟧. [Register the character plot](⟦shared:2⟧) to connect its exact source boundaries.

39.translation: ## Trace an alignment column to the plot ⟦shared:0⟧

40.translation: In this small synthetic example, column three of A is a gap. A known gap has a true ⟦shared:0⟧ flag and a missing ⟦shared:1⟧. The absent fifth column returns false. Only observed source positions can be passed to the display lookup.
